name: usb_c_sink
summary: USB-C receptacle as a USB 2.0 sink: 5 V from the host, D+/D-, and Rd on each CC pin
note: A device that only takes power and USB 2.0 data. Each CC pin has its own 5.1 kohm pull-down (Rd) so the source turns VBUS on whichever way the plug is turned; the two must not share one resistor. 1 % parts meet both the 20 % tolerance that only asks for default power and the 10 % one a sink needs to read the source's advertised current. Both D+ pads and both D- pads are joined at the receptacle, so either plug orientation works. The receptacle's pin names are KiCad 9's (its shield pin is S1; KiCad 10 calls it SH). No ESD protection: add it on boards a person plugs by hand often.

VBUS.note: The host's 5 V. Default USB power's range is the USB 2.0 specification's (not read); 4.75-5.5 V unloaded is what a Type-C Current source must give, and up to 5.5 V is what a legacy device may see at light load

usb.note: The cable's far end is a host, so a device's USB connects here.

citations.quote: Both CC1 and CC2 pins shall be independently terminated to ground through Rd.

citations.note: The column is whether the sink can detect the source's power capability; the ±10 % 5.1 kΩ row says Yes.

citations.quote: The allowable default range for VBUS as measured at the Source receptacle shall be as defined by the USB 2.0 and USB 3.2 specifications.
shall output a voltage in the range of 4.75 V – 5.5 V when no current is being drawn
